extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians (graduate students, postdocs, junior faculty) considering what to publish and how it affects career/job talks
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for mathematicians on which results to publish and how to shape a coherent research publication record that supports talks and job-market success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve major open problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The clearest path to publishable work is resolving significant unsolved questions; these stand alone without needing broader narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority publish results that solve important open problems — such work is self-evidently publishable and does not require being framed as part of a larger story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a coherent research story
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than scattered contributions, develop 'a series' of interconnected papers that collectively advance understanding. 'You start your talk by telling what's the state of the sub-area' and show how your work fits this arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a sequence of papers with a recognizable theme so talks and job-market presentations tell a unified narrative rather than a patchwork of unrelated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publications can damage your reputation. A strong job talk requires coherence, not 'a patchwork quilt' of disparate papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing many minor or low-impact papers just to increase counts; a smaller number of substantial, coherent contributions is preferable for hiring committees and professional reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper advance your main research story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing, ask whether the result strengthens or clarifies your ongoing research direction; if not, consider holding off or integrating it into a larger project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Will it be discoverable and useful to others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results that other researchers will find and use; consider whether the problem and methods connect to an active community or subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the paper provides a substantive new idea or result rather than a marginal tweak or repetitive variation on existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you explain its significance in a compelling colloquium talk?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot present the result as part of a clear, engaging talk that explains its importance, it may not be worth publishing on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish one-off results unrelated to your primary research direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid one-off results unrelated to your primary research direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing isolated findings that don't fit your main narrative can dilute your research profile and make your portfolio look incoherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish to inflate publication counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work published purely to inflate publication counts is discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic harms: seeking quantity over substance harms reputation and can negatively affect job prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid low-quality or predatory venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to low-quality or predatory venues should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing in dubious venues can reflect poorly on you; prefer reputable journals and conferences even if that means fewer publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware negative impact of mediocre work
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediocre work can have 'negative impact on your job search,' as evaluators assess publication portfolios' coherence and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the signaling effect of each publication: mediocre or fragmented output can hurt rather than help when hiring committees evaluate you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic selection as a quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Which results are worth publishing at all is itself a quality signal: 'Good math' includes a strategic dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the decision to publish as part of your professional judgment; selective, well-chosen publications convey discernment and higher standards.
